title.value: The Responsible Foundation Model Development Cheatsheet : A Review of Tools & Resources
title.justification: The title provides a comprehensive summary of the paper's content, focusing on the review and compilation of tools and resources aimed at the responsible development of foundation models.
title.quote: To help shape responsible development practices, we introduce the Foundation Model Development Cheatsheet: a growing collection of 250+ tools and resources spanning text, vision, and speech modalities.

analysis.description: This paper presents a comprehensive guide for the development of foundation models, offering a collection of over 250 tools and resources aimed at supporting ethical and responsible practices across various aspects of AI development including data sourcing, model training, evaluation, and deployment. It identifies gaps and provides recommendations for improvement in existing tools.

type.justification: The paper surveys existing resources and tools, and provides recommendations based on empirical observations in the AI development ecosystem.
type.quote: To address these gaps, we conduct a focused survey, not of scientific literature (which already exists for many FM development topics), but of resources for FM development such as datasets, software packages, documentation, guides, frameworks, and practical tools.

name.justification: The paper focuses on tools and practices that contribute to ethical and responsible development within the AI field, particularly for foundational models.
name.quote: To help shape responsible development practices, we introduce the Foundation Model Development Cheatsheet: a growing collection of 250+ tools and resources spanning text, vision, and speech modalities.

name.justification: The paper covers ethical implications and responsibilities related to AI model development, particularly concerning data documentation and governance.
name.quote: 'Tools for data sourcing, model evaluation, and monitoring are critically under-serving ethical and real-world needs.'

name.justification: The paper includes tools and resources related to text modalities, indicating a significant focus on natural language processing.

name.justification: CommonCrawl is frequently referenced as a key source for text pretraining data, indicative of its prominent use in the survey.
name.quote: In the text domain, web scrapes from common crawl (commoncrawl.org), or OSCAR (https://oscar-project.org/) (Suárez et al., 2019; Laippala et al., 2022) are the base ingredient for most pretraining corpora.

referenced_paper_title.value: Quality at a Glance: An Audit of Web-Crawled Multilingual Datasets
referenced_paper_title.justification: The referenced papers discuss the use and implications of using CommonCrawl data footprints widely recognized in web-crawled datasets for AI training.
referenced_paper_title.quote: Quality at a glance: An audit of web-crawled multilingual datasets. Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics, 10:50–72, 2022.

name.justification: The paper consistently refers to Oscar as a primary resource for multilingual text datasets which are essential for training.
name.quote: In the text domain, web scrapes from common crawl (commoncrawl.org), or OSCAR (https://oscar-project.org/) (Suárez et al., 2019; Laippala et al., 2022) are the base ingredient for most pretraining corpora.

referenced_paper_title.value: Towards Better Structured and Less Noisy Web Data: Oscar with Register Annotations
referenced_paper_title.justification: The paper on Oscar provides essential details about the strides taken to improve the dataset's structuring and annotation for better use in training AI models.
referenced_paper_title.quote: Towards better structured and less noisy web data: Oscar with register annotations. In Proceedings of the Eighth Workshop on Noisy User-generated Text (W-NUT 2022), pages 215–221, 2022.

name.justification: The Pile is a known large-scale dataset encompassing diverse sources, prominently featured in discussions about pretraining data.
name.quote: This includes the Pile (Gao et al., 2020), RefinedWeb (Penedo et al., 2023), RedPajama (Together AI, 2023), and Dolma (Soldaini et al., 2024), which have iterated on basic document quality filtering and deduplication.

referenced_paper_title.value: The Pile: An 800GB Dataset of Diverse Text for Language Modeling
referenced_paper_title.justification: The reference paper elaborates on the dataset's variety and comprehensive nature for language modeling, which the cheatsheet paper highlights.
referenced_paper_title.quote: The pile: An 800gb dataset of diverse text for language modeling. arXiv preprint arXiv:2101.00027, 2020.

name.justification: LibriVox is used as a prominent source of English audiobook data for foundational model evaluation in speech modalities.
name.quote: In the context of speech, webscrapes of English audiobook data from LibriVox (a website hosting free public domain audiobooks) are commonly used for foundation model architecture development and evaluation.

referenced_paper_title.value: Libri-Light: A benchmark for ASR with limited or no supervision
referenced_paper_title.justification: The referenced paper explores LibriVox's utility in training models, particularly under constraints of limited supervision.
referenced_paper_title.quote: Libri-light: A benchmark for ASR with limited or no supervision. In ICASSP 2020-2020 IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech and Signal Processing (ICASSP), pages 7669–7673. IEEE, 2020.

name.justification: ImageNet is a foundational benchmark dataset for image classification, highlighted for its historical significance and use in benchmarking tasks.
name.quote: In the context of vision, there are a few well-known data sources for finetuning. ImageNet (Deng et al., 2009) provides the historical framework for which image classification models competed on 1.3M samples with 1000 diverse classes.

referenced_paper_title.value: ImageNet: A Large-Scale Hierarchical Image Database
referenced_paper_title.justification: ImageNet's significance and foundational role in computer vision is deeply explored in the associated paper, highlighting its benchmark status.
referenced_paper_title.quote: Imagenet: A large-scale hierarchical image database. In 2009 IEEE Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition, pages 248–255, 2009.

name.justification: The paper frequently mentions Hugging Face Datasets as a major catalog for both pretraining and finetuning datasets across various domains and tasks.
name.quote: HuggingFace Datasets (https://huggingface.co/docs/datasets/index) offers the largest and most popular AI community catalog across modalities and tasks.

referenced_paper_title.value: Datasets: A Community Library for Natural Language Processing
referenced_paper_title.justification: The paper discusses the broad utility and reach of Hugging Face Datasets in being a central resource for dataset storage and sharing in NLP and expanding domains.
